Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-28 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~1h15m
Participants: Aaron, Priya, Diego, Maya, Xavier, Lia, Omar, Samira, Ben

Summary (auto): quick sync about staged rollout choreography for Private beta, oncall handbook draft, canary windows and fallback policies. Some auto-transcribe glitches (V P C vs VPC, K V cache).

00:00 Aaron: alright folks, thanks for joining on time, we'll run about 75 minutes, goal is to land the choreography and the handbook owner, and leave with clear next steps. um, anyone has to drop early?
00:12 Priya: I can stay the whole time, but heads up I'm oncall tonight so I might step out if an alert pops.
00:18 Maya: same, calendar + child pickup at 3:15 but should be fine.
00:24 Diego: good. quick note, infra just finished the scheduler patch for fractional slices.
00:32 Aaron: excellent, first topic — staged rollout choreography. Lia, you had suggestions on cadence?
00:40 Lia: yeah, so thinking three slices: 0.5%, 5%, 25% over two days each, with 24‑hour observation windows. But we should allow accelerated ramp if latency and error rates are stable. also need an explicit canary kill criteria.
01:05 Samira: for oncall ops, we need both automated thresholds and human checkboxes. automated e.g. 95th percentile latency increase > 20% or token error spikes above baseline. human checks include spot‑checks for hallucination regressions on our eval prompts.
01:24 Xavier: can we codify the hallucination checks? Our eval harness is in the repo but it's not wired to the canary pipeline.
01:34 Priya: we can add a webhook from the eval runner to post results into the canary dashboard. Diego, infra, any barriers?
01:42 Diego: nope, webhook's fine. question is storage and retention for those eval traces, need to check compliance but for internal beta it's okay.
01:52 Omar: on the V P C side, customers sometimes ask for single‑tenant routing, we need to verify the P R O X Y rules won't throttle small slices — there was an odd interaction last test.
02:06 Aaron: note that in the runbook as 'proxy throttling caveat'. Diego, add a note.
02:12 Diego: will do.
02:16 Ben: on QA side, we'll need a concise checklist: success criteria, roll forward vs rollback triggers, manual sign‑off gating. we'll draft and share.
02:28 Aaron: perfect. Next: oncall handbook. Maya, you created the draft, walk us through the key changes.
02:35 Maya: thanks. main changes — simplified escalation ladder (oncall -> SRE -> infra -> exec), added a 'who owns fallback' section, and included step‑by‑step canary rollback commands. i've also added a short 'what to look for' for KV cache — some of the terms in the auto transcript are K V cache but that means prefix/KV cache evictions and warmup.
03:00 Samira: the escalation ladder looks good; question about who paginates when the canary goes sideways: the oncall person should page the SE who worked on the change, and the handbook lists the SE contact matrix.
03:12 Priya: also adding clear instructions for when to toggle prefix cache bypass, because we saw a scenario where cache warmup caused latency tail spikes. toggle path in runbook must include metrics to watch (cache hit rate, tail latency).
03:31 Diego: add runbook snippet to failover to a compatible quantized model variant — we tested fallback kernels last week. there are subtle differences in output formatting so QA must be aware.
03:46 Ben: yep we'll include formatting checks too.
03:50 Lia: on communications — we need a single Slack channel for the canary with pinned runbook and a status page update template. Aaron, can you own notify to CS?
03:58 Aaron: yeah I'll own internal comms. I'll also coordinate Sales notifications for existing Dedicated customers.
04:06 Xavier: small nit: the telemetry retention for canary traces — who has access? we need to limit PII.
04:12 Omar: platform will mask user text in traces; retention will be 30 days for beta and 90 for GA unless compliance requires otherwise.
04:24 Priya: about KV/prefix cache perf tests — i'm proposing a two‑part test: cold startup evictions and steady state QPS. results feed into canary gating. Diego will help run infra‑side, and Ben will validate.
04:42 Diego: agreed. i'll schedule a low‑traffic window early next week.
04:46 Ben: and QA will run a regression set during that window.
04:50 Aaron: rollback policies — Diego, give us the simple decision tree.
04:55 Diego: okay, step one: automated trigger fires (latency/error thresholds), step two: quick human review within 15 minutes, step three: if confirmed, activate model fallback to quantized compatible variant and scale slices back to 0.5% while debugging. if backend fails, full rollback and traffic shift to hosted endpoints.
05:17 Priya: add to that: when fallback occurs, we must capture KV cache snapshot and shipping it to the debugging bucket, also flag correlating traces.
05:27 Maya: where do we document who pulls the plug? the handbook says oncall triggers, but the execs want a manual confirmation for >25% impact.
05:36 Samira: agreed, make manual confirmation required for >25% user impact. smaller impact — SRE can proceed.
05:45 Aaron: noted. next, dependency check — any blockers?
05:50 Priya: SSO and KMS keys are in place for the private beta, but we need KMS rotation policy documented for the handbook. Omar?
05:59 Omar: yes, KMS rotation policy is being updated. i'll add a short FAQ in the handbook referencing the KMS rotation cadence.
06:06 Xavier: did we mention fallbacks for model quant skew? last sprint we saw small semantic drift when switching quantized variants.
06:15 Diego: that's why we have the output formatting QA step and a light semantic regression harness — we need to make sure it's in the canary gating.
06:25 Ben: QA will run the semantic harness after each slice ramp. it's lightweight but catches big regressions.
06:32 Lia: timeline — do we think we can start slice 1 canary May 10?
06:38 Aaron: tentative yes. need handbook finalized, canary window scheduled, and the KV perf tests run.
06:44 Maya: i'll push the handbook draft today and assign reviewers.
06:48 Priya: i'll schedule the tests for May 5th and the canary for May 10th low window.
06:54 Diego: infra will be oncall for the canary. i'll prepare the proxy caveat note.
07:00 Samira: i'll update the oncall rota and set the paging matrix.
07:06 Aaron: perfect. any final questions?
07:10 Lia: small ask — add a short 'postmortem template' to the handbook for canary incidents.
07:18 Maya: will do.
07:22 Aaron: great. recap of next steps (auto): Maya publish handbook, Priya run KV tests, Diego fallback runbook, Ben QA checklist, Aaron coordinate comms. we'll reconvene in one week if blockers persist. thanks everyone.
07:40 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: periodic mis‑recognitions for acronyms — V P C, K V cache, S L A — are present. occasional speaker attribution may be approximate.
